title: Late-stage congestion hotspot resolved via localized pin optimization
design_context: 7nm node, 1.2M placeable instances, 95 macros, 3 clock domains, commercial P&R
observation: Congestion overflow of 14.5% in top-left quadrant, 3 metal layers showing >10% overflow, no DRC violations but routing estimated to fail at 12% overflow threshold
hypothesis: Macro M17 placement created a routing channel bottleneck that global placement couldn't resolve without violating timing

candidates_considered.action: Re-run global placement with congestion-aware cost weight increased from 0.3 to 0.8
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Adds 2 days to schedule with no guarantee the hotspot will resolve given macro positions are fixed

candidates_considered.action: Insert congestion-guided buffers in hotspot region
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Increases area by 0.4% and degrades IR drop by 3mV, risking hold violations on 12 identified paths

candidates_considered.action: Swap macros M17 and M23 to open routing channel
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Requires re-running timing for both macro domains (estimated 1.2 days CPU) and risks breaking existing timing closure

chosen_intervention: Local pin access optimization on 18 cells in hotspot + 8% halo expansion around M17, followed by incremental detailed routing
expert_assessment: Correct call for schedule constraints. Lesson: congestion hotspots near macros often yield to local pin access changes before resorting to global re-placement. Does not transfer to blocks with >90% utilization where local fixes are insufficient.
weakest_point: The exact congestion overflow reduction from pin access optimization alone is uncertain without a real tool run

title: Clock skew signature distinguishes physical problem from constraint issue
design_context: 28nm node, 800K placeable instances, 60 macros, 2 clock domains, commercial P&R
observation: 8200 timing paths failing by 20-45ps each, all sharing clock domain CLK_A, slack distribution tightly clustered (std dev 8ps), no common endpoint logic
hypothesis: Excessive clock skew on CLK_A network due to unbalanced buffering, creating systematic timing failure across the domain

candidates_considered.action: Relax setup constraint on CLK_A by 50ps
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Would mask real timing issues in paths not affected by skew, risking silicon failure in other domains

candidates_considered.action: Upsize all drivers on failing paths
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Increases area by 0.6% and power by 2.1%, plus creates new congestion in already-tight regions
Requires 3 days of runtime and could introduce new timing violations while not addressing root cause

chosen_intervention: Re-run clock tree synthesis for CLK_A with skew target reduced from 50ps to 25ps, followed by incremental timing optimization on top 100 failing paths
expert_assessment: Excellent diagnosis from signature. The tight slack clustering was the giveaway for clock network issue. Lesson: always plot slack histogram before diving into logic fixes. Would not have worked if the issue was actually a constraint problem.
weakest_point: The exact skew reduction achievable without area increase is tool-dependent

title: Async block boundary budget derived from measured clock uncertainty
design_context: 7nm node, Block Alpha: 1.5M instances, Block Beta: 0.8M instances, async boundary, commercial P&R
observation: 210 paths crossing Alpha-Beta boundary failing by 80-200ps, all failures occur in setup check from Alpha to Beta
hypothesis: Missing or incorrectly derived timing budget at async boundary; current SDC assumes zero skew which is unrealistic for this clock network topology

candidates_considered.action: Set fixed budget of 10% of Beta clock period (500ps) for all boundary paths
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Overly conservative for most paths, would cause unnecessary optimization effort and area increase estimated at 1.2%

candidates_considered.action: Mark all boundary paths as false paths
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Would break functional timing for real synchronous paths and cause silicon failure on boundary registers

candidates_considered.action: Use clock latency difference only as budget
candidates_considered.rejected_because: Ignores clock uncertainty and jitter, which account for ~60ps of the observed failures

chosen_intervention: Derived budget = measured_clock_skew(120ps) + max_uncertainty(40ps) + 10% margin(16ps) = 176ps; applied as set_clock_uncertainty -setup 176ps on boundary
expert_assessment: Textbook budget derivation. The key was measuring actual clock skew rather than relying on theoretical max. Lesson: always verify clock network metrics before deriving boundary budgets. Method fails if clock networks are not yet stable.
weakest_point: The margin percentage (10%) is arbitrary and tool/flow-dependent
